sources_considered.why: Direct measurement of generated search summaries, with collection dates and methods.
Primary disclosure of a personal agent and proposed everyday organizational uses; does not independently establish reliability.
Dated evaluation of everyday delegated tasks, including repeated trials and explicit limitations.

evidence_items.locator: Findings on AI-summary frequency and length; methodology dates result collection to April 7–17, 2025
evidence_items.explanation: Directly observed prose-length search summaries support the search-output component. Length alone does not establish writing quality or the stronger interpretation of consistently reliable answers.

evidence_items.locator: Opening description, following the school-email and permission-slip example
evidence_items.explanation: Google describes an agent for organizational chores, including school-email deadlines, itineraries and calendar arrangements. These advertised capabilities are relevant progress, but the announcement does not measure successful completion or reliability.

receipt.public_excerpt: 31% of tasks passed once were failed on another try.

evidence_items.explanation: The evaluation reports successful everyday task execution alongside inconsistent repeated performance; its detailed denominator is assistant-task pairs that succeeded at least once. Its small, simulated task set does not establish dependable life organization, and failures cannot contradict eventual arrival.

unresolved_gaps: The reviewed evidence does not establish dependable management across a person's schedules, tasks and everyday arrangements in repeated real-world use.
The search measurement documents summaries but does not directly grade their writing quality or factual reliability.
Marcus supplies no threshold that cleanly separates useful organizational assistance from an agent that can 'organize lives'.
No decisive event establishes both components under the stated reading, and the forecast has no deadline.
